dod_intent_evidence: Two Office for Chemical and Biological Defense Phase II SBIR awards ($853,547 in 2022, $740,805 in 2023) plus their own 'About' page states 'revenue is derived primarily through R&D contracting with DoD' — SBIR abstracts + homepage.
score_evidence: "Advance warning of chemical and biological (CB) threats is of critical importance to our warfighters" and "Autonomous retraining based on observed conditions... is critical to deploying a battlefield capability rather than a post-processing detection capability" → shows this company is already fluent in operator/battlefield framing, lowering deployment_awareness_absence and operator_absence per the 'fluent = low score, still a keep' calibration rule

blind_spots.blind_spot: No ATO/RMF/CMMC/ITAR language anywhere on the public site despite the company's own claim that DoD is its primary revenue source and it also sells the same lidar tech commercially to oil & gas.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A dual-use company selling identical lidar hardware to commercial oil & gas customers and to DoD CBD program offices needs a visible ITAR/export-control and CMMC compliance story — none is public, meaning it's untested against the exact compliance gate that stalls many small subcontractors before fielding.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Public website is written for both commercial and government audiences without segmentation; compliance messaging may exist internally but isn't surfaced.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Revenue is derived primarily through R&D contracting with DoD and federal agencies involved in atmospheric and environmental sensing, as well as commercial sensing activities focused on the oil and gas industry.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Their own abstract trains and validates the plume-detection ML model on data from Dugway Proving Ground, which the same abstract explicitly calls a 'stable, low-clutter environment' — the opposite of the real battlefield target environment.
blind_spots.operator_reality: The abstract itself states the real target is 'a battlefield or other active environment where hundreds or thousands of aerosol plumes may be generated every day' — a high-clutter setting the training data doesn't represent, which is exactly the kind of lab-to-field generalization gap that kills programs at transition.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Government test ranges like DPG are the standard, most accessible place to collect labeled plume data; collecting labeled data in an actual contested environment is operationally very hard.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: S3 has previously shown that a Support Vector Machine (SVM) supervised learning ML model can distinguish disseminated from non-disseminated plumes at a high rate of accuracy in a stable, low-clutter environment such as that typically found at Dugway Proving Ground (DPG).

blind_spots.blind_spot: Abstract language is entirely sensor-system and data-pipeline focused ('networked environment,' 'sensor networks,' 'data products') and never names the human decision-maker who reads the alert and acts on it.
blind_spots.operator_reality: "Decisions... of our forces" is passive — the abstract never says who makes that call, on what device, in what time window, wearing what PPE, which is the actual adoption bottleneck for a CBD detection tool.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Team is sensor-physics and ML engineers; human-factors/CONOPS work for the alert-to-decision handoff isn't their core competency.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: These 3D images can be combined with the plume measurements to provide an improved picture of the threat environment for decisions regarding force protections and maneuverability of our forces.

opener_hook: S3's two CBD Phase II SBIRs train plume-detection ML on Dugway Proving Ground's low-clutter range — the same abstract calls real battlefields 'high-clutter' by comparison.
what_they_do: Makes standoff lidar/UV-Raman sensors for chemical-biological threat and aerosol-plume detection, funded by two DoD Chemical & Bio Defense Phase II SBIRs, alongside commercial environmental-sensing products for oil & gas.
